name: Buja Online Data Center
notes: Official site describes a local Bujumbura data center offering VPS, web hosting, fiber internet and IT hardware services; Datacenters.com also lists it in Bujumbura Mairie.

name: Burundi Backbone System Datacenter
notes: Data-center directories list a BBS datacenter at 20 Boulevard Mwambutsa, Quartier Kigobe, Bujumbura; no public capacity found.

name: Lacell SU Burundi / Smart Burundi data center
notes: Directories list a Bujumbura facility on Boulevard de l'Independance. Status is marked unknown because public telecom records indicate Smart/Lacell SU's mobile operation was shut down in 2022 while facility directories still list the site.

name: Central Bank of Burundi main data centre modernization
developer: Banque de la Republique du Burundi / BAIP group / NRD
notes: BAIP/INVL reported completion of BRB critical IT infrastructure and data migration; the project covered the main data centre at the Central Bank head office in Bujumbura, plus Ngozi DR and Gitega branch infrastructure.

name: Burundi Digital Foundations national physical data hosting solution
developer: Government of Burundi / SETIC / World Bank
notes: World Bank project documentation includes preparation of specifications for a new physical data hosting solution, i.e. a data center, and the Burundi finance ministry's 2026 PAFEN update names a national data center as a priority. Exact site is not public; assigned to Bujumbura Mairie because the program is tied to central government digital infrastructure.

name: Ministry of Health national data center roadmap
developer: Ministry of Public Health and Fight Against AIDS / Government of Burundi
notes: World Bank DE4A Burundi assessment says the PNDIS II health informatics plan includes establishment of a data center within the Ministry of Health; exact ministry site/capacity not stated.

name: Central Bank of Burundi Gitega branch IT infrastructure
developer: Banque de la Republique du Burundi / BAIP group / NRD
notes: BRB data centre infrastructure modernization was implemented across three sites, including a Gitega branch. Source does not identify this branch as the disaster-recovery site; capacity not public.
